author: bpandola
body:
For a number of Query protocol-based services (e.g. Cloud Formation, Redshift, SNS), the original `boto` library would add a `ContentType=JSON` parameter to the request, which would cause the AWS backend to return JSON instead of the default XML normally used by the protocol.  When `botocore`/`boto3` came on the scene, they dropped this optional parameter and only supported XML responses for these services.  There was a bit of a painful transition for `moto` during this time, as it had to support both `boto` and `boto3` (see #402, #444, https://github.com/getmoto/moto/commit/3cdb4afad0f6a42c790c39c56e2b6f0680d54ff7).

Direct support for the `boto` library was dropped from `moto` long ago, but the code supporting both JSON and XML responses for some service backends remains.  The `ContentType=JSON` parameter is a limited use-case that (as far as I can tell) was only ever used by the the original `boto` library. I don't believe any current SDKs make use of this parameter, but I have confirmed that it is still supported by the AWS backend.

Despite the limited usefulness, it just wasn't that much work to implement a `QueryJSONSerializer`, so this PR adds support for it to aid in migrating the aforementioned services to our new core serialization code.

Some gadgets provide some fields that can be quite big (cwd, exepath, etc).
In some scenarios it's needed to change their maximum size to save memory.
This commit completes the work initiated in  ("gadgets/trace_dns: Use optional fields on socket enricher")
by setting the size of the fields in the event structure according to the
configuration of the socker enricher. This is done by creating a new BTF
spec with the modified structures and passing it as a target relocation.

Support for this in all gadgets (not only fields from the socker enricher)
will be added in another commit later on.

### Discussion

I'm not sure this approach is worth it. Even if it optimizes the gadgets by reducing the size of the event they send to userspace, it's sub-optimal as a lot of trash is sent to userspace, perhaps better to fix #3491 rather than introducing this temporal and complicated solution.

```bash
$ sudo ig run trace_dns --verify-image=false --paths --fields cwd,exepath,proc.comm,proc.creds.uid --socket-enricher-fields="cwd=512,exepath=512"
```

`FC.optionalNullable FC.EmitNull selector giantObjectSchema` would cause `giantObjectSchema` to be inlined at the use site, i.e. in the object where optionalNullable was invoked.

This duplication of the encoding of `GiantObject` is unnecessary, since we *can* mark any named schema as
nullable, by having it be the sole inhabitant of e.g. a `oneOf`.

In fact, this structure is proposed by the [official Swagger
editor](https://editor.swagger.io): For example if you try put `nullable` next
to `$ref`, it will note that it is invalid, and suggest using `oneOf`.

So in this PR, we instead generate this slightly awkward encoding, which I
consider an improvement since it avoids inlining at every use site.

## **Description**


Currently, when a user clicks the "Notifications" link in the Global menu, the Wallet Notifications permissions modal is shown (instead of taking them over to the Notifications page).

However, if the user has "ThirdPartyNotifySnaps" installed, we do NOT show this modal, and instead, we navigate to the Notifications page.

I think we should change this so that when the user clicks the Notifications link (in the Metamask menu or via the notifications deep link) it ALWAYS takes them to the Notifications page, but it would _also_ display the Wallet Notification Settings modal if they are NOT opted in AND don't have "ThirdPartyNotifySnaps". If they have opted in OR have "ThirdPartyNotifySnaps" we do NOT show the modal.

Playing out some scenarios using the new logic I'm proposing above:

Scenario 1:
* user does NOT have wallet permissions enabled
* user does NOT have "ThirdPartyNotifySnaps" installed
* user clicks [link.metamask.io/notifications](http://link.metamask.io/notifications)
* we navigate to the notifications page AND immediately show the Wallet Notification Permissions modal.

Scenario 2:
* user does NOT have wallet permissions enabled
* user has "ThirdPartyNotifySnaps" installed
* user clicks [link.metamask.io/notifications](http://link.metamask.io/notifications)
* we navigate to the notifications page; we do NOT show the modal

Scenario 3:
* user does have wallet permissions enabled
* user clicks [link.metamask.io/notifications](http://link.metamask.io/notifications)
* we navigate to the notifications page; we do NOT show the permissions modal

So that is what this PR does. Thoughts?

## Summary

Allows Counterfact to run with no transpilation when the runtime natively supports TypeScript type stripping (e.g. `tsx`, `ts-node`, or Node.js with `--experimental-strip-types`). Rather than requiring a CLI flag, the server probes the runtime at startup and automatically serves routes directly from the `routes/` directory when native TypeScript execution is available, falling back to the existing `.cache`-based transpilation otherwise.

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

The goal is to allow running Counterfact with no transpilation at all. In my tests so far you can run this with TSX directly against the `routes` folder, no need for `.cache`.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [x] When running with `tsx` (e.g. `tsx src/app.ts`) or `node --experimental-strip-types`, the server starts without creating a `.cache` directory and serves routes directly from `routes/`
- [x] When running with standard `node` (no TypeScript support), the server creates and uses a `.cache/` directory for transpiled output, matching prior behavior
- [x] TypeScript route handlers are executed correctly in native TS mode (type annotations do not cause runtime errors)
- [x] Existing routes and behavior are unchanged when running in the default (non-native TS) execution mode
- [x] Switching from a native-TS runtime to a standard Node runtime (or vice versa) does not break the server or leave stale cache artifacts

## Tasks

- Implement `runtimeCanExecuteErasableTs()` in `src/util/runtime-can-execute-erasable-ts.ts` — writes a temporary `.ts` probe file and attempts to `import()` it to detect runtime capability
- Replace the `useTsx` config option with the automatic runtime detection in `app.ts`
- Conditionally skip transpiler startup and `.cache` cleanup when native TS execution is detected
- Treat `.ts` files as ES modules in `src/server/determine-module-kind.ts`
- Add a unit test for `runtimeCanExecuteErasableTs`
